non_blocking: OPEN LANDING GATE, not satisfied by this PASS: the quorum round-2 carve-out (gpt6-1-sol, verbatim) makes an x86_64 disagreement BLOCK landing. The x86_64 golden was copied from the arm64 recording (as 0f5a1175 did) and NOT independently recorded on x86_64, and the confirming fast-tier run could not be exercised here: the clone's origin is a local path and 'gh pr list' reports 'none of the git remotes configured for this repository point to a known GitHub host'. The sprint's own MS3 record says 'Post-push gh pr checks: not run (no push per executor brief)'. The controller must run the PR's 'make ci-fast' on ubuntu-latest before landing and must NOT regenerate an architecture-specific golden if it disagrees.

The ci-fast edge itself is unprotected (mutant 2). Deleting the single 'ci-fast: replay-map-index' line removes MapIndex from the fast tier, and nothing in the repo detects the loss: 'make -n ci-fast' still exits 0. The failure mode is exactly the nightly-red this row exists to fix, and the nightly 'make test' (tools-test -> MapIndex) would still catch a bad fixture, so this is a durability gap, not a correctness hole. The repo already has the precedent for closing it - 7ah's 'similar-main-guard' is a real guard target that runs inside ci-fast (Makefile:115) - so a 'map-index-guard' asserting that ci-fast carries the MapIndex step would close the loop.

The control's expected string hard-codes the live catalogue index: assertIn("earth_log_voyage.ndjson:3 plan CNS5:3627 index 1, stars.json 2", bad). After a catalogue reorder the fix is NOT only a 0f5a1175-style re-record, as the design's Risks states; the control's expected string must be updated too (mutant 3 shows the message becomes 'stars.json 3'). The failure is loud (red at the PR), never silent, but the design's remediation text understates the work.

n in the control is a raw text count of the literal '"index":2,"id":"CNS5:3627"' over the whole log text, while len(bad) counts plan intents. They agree today (6 = 6, verified) because every occurrence is a plan intent. A future log carrying that literal in a non-plan context (a 'star' row, a comment, a different intent kind) would make n > len(bad) and fail the control spuriously. Fails loudly, narrow hypothetical, and the same coupling already exists in the inherited controls 'test_a_stale_index_fails' and 'test_an_unknown_id_fails' (both go red with '7 != 1' under mutant 3), so this is the house pattern rather than a 7ai regression.

The changelog fragment says the control 'fails unless exactly those six are reported as mismatches', but the test deliberately computes n dynamically rather than hard-coding 6 (the design's risk section says so on purpose). The prose is accurate today and goes stale if a log is added or removed; 'exactly the n plan lines that carry the index-2 literal' would be the durable phrasing.

Scope note for the reader, not a defect: the guard proves that every COMMITTED replay log plans each star at its stars.json index. It says nothing about the ALPHA constants that still carry '{"index": 1, "id": "CNS5:3627"}' in 8 GDScript files, sim/stops_test.ail and tools/worlds_leak.py (design follow-up F1, deliberately out of scope). GalaxyMap.target_name()/subtitle_text() show the common name only when catalogue[index].id == id, so a capture driven by one of those constants may read 'CNS5:3627' where the live game reads 'Alpha Centauri A'. The design's F1 hypothesis remains unmeasured and this sprint did not test it.

summary: Independent cross-vendor evaluation of sprint R1-7AI-EARTH-LOG-MAP-INDEX (base e0ba4ae7, head c1af429f). All 11 acceptance criteria were independently re-verified rather than taken on record, including the two red baselines, which I reconstructed from a base tree extracted with 'git archive' (AC1: Ran 3 tests, FAILED (failures=3), the exact mismatch line) and from HEAD's control over the base fixture (AC2: Ran 4 tests, FAILED (failures=4), '6 != 5') - so the test-first discipline genuinely held. The decisive piece of evidence for the golden change is that the BASE fixture, re-run on the pinned AILANG v0.56.1, reproduces the OLD golden digest e62a9272... bit-for-bit, while the corrected fixture reproduces the NEW digest 07dcdfc6... and the two 1,389,901-byte state streams differ in exactly the three journey.plan.target.index echoes at offsets 56554, 60660 and 1059580: the golden is a faithful re-record of a genuinely-changed input, not a hand-edit. The single-session replay (VM 43.33 s, interpreter 94.86 s, '1 cases, all identical', rc=0) confirms VM = interpreter = golden. Both committed code blocks are byte-identical to the design's fences, the scope is exactly the nine authorised files, and the do-not-touch list is verifiably respected. Three mutants of my own: the AC8 re-introduction drill is killed (all four tests red, the control firing on '6 != 5'); a simulated catalogue reorder is killed (the guard fires at the fast tier, which also shows the post-reorder fix must edit the control's expected string, not only re-record the golden); and the deletion of the single 'ci-fast: replay-map-index' edge is NOT killed - the fast-tier presence of the guard is itself unprotected, so that wiring can be lost silently and the regression would revert to the nightly-red this row exists to fix. That gap is bounded (the nightly's tools-test still runs MapIndex) and is recorded as the principal non-blocking finding, together with the still-open x86_64 landing gate, which this PASS does NOT satisfy: the x86_64 golden is a copy, the runner's confirmation could not be exercised here (no GitHub remote), and the controller must run the PR's 'make ci-fast' on ubuntu-latest and block landing if the x86_64 replay disagrees. No blocking finding. Score 97, verdict PASS.
